subject: Model fit evals: recommended models, benchmarks, and parity thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model fit evals: next steps & prompt set

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of ask:
- PayGrid wants a short-run evaluation to validate open-model parity vs your proprietary baseline on invoice parsing + routing prompts.
- Primary success metric: label-level F1 parity within 2% of baseline for core invoice fields + human-acceptance signal on downstream routing.

Proposed plan:
1) Redwood provides a recommended model shortlist, prompt set, and a small benchmark harness we use for parity checks.
2) PayGrid runs the harness (or we can run in a redwood-dedicated eval) for 3 business days using your sample corpus.
3) Measure metric deltas, surface qualitative failure modes, then iterate prompts or recommend alternate model variant.

Attachments: prompt set (paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv) and preliminary benchmark doc.

Can you confirm the acceptance threshold above (<=2% F1 delta) and whether PayGrid prefers us to run the eval or to run it yourselves with our harness?

Thanks — I can kick off scheduling once we have that.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

--Attachment: paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv (24KB)
--Attachment: benchmark_open_vs_base_20260617.pdf (320KB)

Date: 2026-06-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals: next steps & prompt set

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. Confirming details from our side: 

- Acceptance: Target is parity within 2% F1 on the main invoice fields. If the delta is 2-5% we treat it as a "near parity" and will accept a short remediation period. Anything >5% will need a deeper review.
- We prefer Redwood to run the eval in a dedicated environment (helps with consistency) but can share the sample corpus and a temporary S3 access.

Next step: Can you run a 3-day eval starting Mon 22nd? We'll share S3 creds by EOD Monday the 19th. Also please add a short kickoff agenda so engineering and product at PayGrid know what to expect.

Emma Liu
Head of Data Science | PayGrid
emma.liu@paygrid.com

Subject: Re: Model fit evals: recommended models, benchmarks, and parity thresholds

Great — we'll run the eval. Quick note on recommended models and why: 

Recommended shortlist (start-to-start):
- Llama-2-13B (quantized variant) — strong instruction-following on structured extraction, good cost/latency tradeoff.
- MPT-30B-Instruct — higher throughput; consider for scale if Llama variant needs more capacity.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (if you want top single-model quality; higher resource needs).

We also recommend trying two tuned prompt families from the attached CSV (paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv): a precise-extraction prompt and a fail-safe prompt that falls back to conservative tagging (reduces false positives).

Benchmark links:
- Preliminary microbenchmarks attached (benchmark_open_vs_base_20260617.pdf) — we ran the shortlist against a small held-out slice from a public invoice corpus to give a sense of deltas.
- Drive folder with harness and scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPayGridEval

Operational notes:
- We'll run the eval in a reserved dedicated pool to match your latency constraints. Aditya will coordinate environment and S3 ingestion.
- Acceptance thresholds noted. We'll output token-level cost and sample failure traces per document to help triage.

Next steps I will take now:
- Schedule kickoff for Mon 2026-06-22 (30m) and share a short agenda (attached).
- Aditya to request S3 creds and confirm ingestion format.

Marissa

--Attachment: eval-run-kickoff-agenda.docx (6KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals: ops notes & parity considerations

Quick ops note / engineering flag for the kickoff: 
- If PayGrid expects inference latency under 350ms p95 for the pipeline, we should prioritize the Llama-2-13B quantized path — it gives the best balance for structured extraction given the token lengths.
- We'll enable prefix caching for repeated vendor templates to reduce cost.
- For parity analysis, recommend we compute both label-level F1 and a human-acceptance pass (sample 100 docs). The human pass usually catches subtle formatting that F1 misses.

Also flag for sales: if parity delta is in the 2-5% "near parity" band, propose a 2-week prompt engineering engagement (fixed-fee) to get within threshold; we'll include a scope estimate in the post-eval report.

-Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
